Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the material placed on record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 26.11.2020 passed by the Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Mahoba in Case Crime No. 477 of 2020 under Section 376, 323, 504 of I.P.C. and Section 3(1)(Da), 3(1)(Dha), 3(2)(5ka) and 3(2)(5) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Kotwali Nagar Mahoba, District Mahoba.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that in this case appellant is innocent and has committed no offence but on account of village rivalry he has been named in this case.

It is also submitted that there is allegation of rape with the victim by the appellant but during medical examination no any such sign was found on her person to show that rape was committed with her by the appellant.
It is also submitted that there is no criminal history against the appellant on the basis of which it cannot be said that appellant has committed the aforesaid offence.
It is further submitted that the appellant is languishing in jail since 27.08.2020.
Learned counsel for the appellant also referred to the amended provisions of SC/ST Act.

All these facts and circumstances were not taken into consideration by the learned Special Judge at the time of considering the bail but rejected it which cannot be said to be lawful, therefore request to set it aside and allow the appeal.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and contended that while tyring to commit rape with the victim the appellant caused injuries on her person and during medical examination all the injuries were found on the body of the victim which support the allegation as made by the victim in the F.I.R.

It is also submitted that the sample was taken and sent to F.S.L. from where report has been obtained which is on record in counter affidavit which also establishes the complicity of the present appellant.
Learned Special Judge S.C./S.T. has considered all these facts while rejecting the bail and there is no any illegality or impropriety in the order but this appeal being devoid of merit

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case submissions made by learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record, the order passed by learned Special Judge,
criminal history against the appellant, the F.S.L. report and also the injuries found on the person of the victim there appears no ground for bail in favour of the appellant and the order passed by learned Special Judge SC/ST Act dated 26.11.2020 cannot be said to be illegal and requires no interference by this Court but this appeal being devoid of merit is hereby dismissed and learned trial court is directed to make its endeavour to proceed with the trial as expeditiously as possible within a period of one year.
Order Date :- 15.2.2024 Suraj Srivastav  Gyan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193598040/
